records.detail: The Banco Central de Sao Tome e Principe publishes its external audit report on its own site. The report on the accounts to 31 December 2024, published 13 February 2026, is on the letterhead of BDO & Associados, SROC, S.A., of Avenida da Republica 50-10, 1069-211 Lisbon, which the report's own footer describes as a Portuguese company and a member of BDO International Limited. The opinion is QUALIFIED, which is unusual for a central bank. The qualification rests on four points. First, the bank's assets include 1,517,669,216 dobras claimed against the State, among them 388,323,250 dobras of interest-free emergency credit granted in 2022 after the floods of late 2021, a 73,500,000 dobra advance in 2024 for fuel imports, 28,169,592 dobras of credits from before 2000 whose contracts provide for interest that has never been recorded, and 657,177,194 dobras owed by the Banco Nacional de Angola under a 1988 banking agreement that the State then used in a settlement with Angola; the auditor says the first two did not meet article 26 of the bank's Organic Law, which capped State borrowing at 5 per cent of the previous year's tax revenue and required settlement within the year, and that the bank asked the State in late 2024 and early 2025 to recognise the debt formally with a repayment plan, which has not happened. Second, a 2022 transfer of 419,911,000 dobras of construction in progress for the bank's new head office included about 34,674,000 dobras advanced to a contractor whose contract the bank terminated in 2017 for non-performance. Third, the bank's 61.1 per cent holding in the payments company SPAUT is carried at 33,491,704 dobras while SPAUT's own equity had fallen to 3,756,626 dobras, so the auditor says an impairment of about 31,000,000 dobras should have been booked. Fourth, 43,192,500 dobras remain receivable from Energy Bank STP, whose licence the central bank cancelled in January 2022. The auditor concludes that assets and equity are overstated.
